evidence: Modifies P2P message deserialization to enforce strict weight and input/output limits on incoming blocks and transactions before full parsing.
rationale: Failing fast during P2P deserialization closes worst-case memory and CPU exhaustion vectors from untrusted peers. A peer can currently send a 4 MB block message containing up to 400,000 zero-input/zero-output transactions that trigger separate CTransaction allocations, or up to 16M weight, all fully deserialized before validation rejects them.
